l2_final.verdict: source-supported conditional resource-exhaustion effect; ordinary third-party app reachability insufficient; not a confirmed app vulnerability.
checks: Public IPCObjectProxy::GetSessionNameForPidUid writes caller-supplied uid/pid and directly calls SendRequestInner with GET_SESSION_NAME_PID_UID; generic SendRequest rejects codes above MAX_TRANSACTION_ID.

The receiving special handler requires local calling plus receiver-process IsSamgrCall flag, rejects only remotePid equal to actual caller PID, then uses parcel uid/pid to create session name and request grant. IsSamgrCall is receiver process state, not caller UID/token ACL.

SoftBus dynamic permission list is one process-global list capped at 100. Capacity is checked before duplicate lookup; full pool rejects subsequent grants including duplicate retries. Entries preserve requested uid/pid and later permission checks match the exact pair. Existing entries are not deleted by pool-full failure; cleanup uses remove/delete or service restart.

SoftBus grant checks the calling IPC token then consumes parcel uid/pid/name. This review did not independently bind the policy implementation/product SAMGR identity, so does not assume the token always passes.
l2_final.existing_test_coverage: Reviewed IPC stub handler/gate tests, helper mock tests, DBinder softbus client refcount mocks, and DSoftBus permission parameter tests. minimum_missing_evidence: Target product build/export/policy evidence that an unprivileged app can obtain a usable registry proxy, invoke this helper, and reach this special dispatch.

Authorized isolated integration evidence that the service token passes the SoftBus gate and pool saturation causes an observable failure for a new legitimate pair, with normal cleanup restoring service.
l2_final.no_action: Do not promote a scanner finding, claim ordinary app exploitability, duplicate a detector solely due to shared DBinderGrantPermission sink, or run an attack PoC.

conditional_observation.claim: Each successful exported GET_SESSION_NAME call makes the target service ask SAMGR to grant that service's own fixed UID/PID session name. IPC mapSessionRefCount increments once per grant. RemoveSessionName decrements only through client/server socket shutdown callbacks, not per query; repeated queries or failed/incomplete lifecycles may leave extra same-name IPC references.
conditional_observation.counterevidence: A normal successful databus socket lifecycle may pair a grant with one shutdown removal. Local unpinned DSoftBus deduplicates same-name grants, and no unique-slot exhaustion or cross-subject authorization effect is evidenced.
conditional_observation.limitations: Ordinary third-party SDK access policy, exact target-paired SoftBus behavior, persistent permission effect, and material attacker-observable impact remain unbound.
